record.paper_title: 20 Open Questions About Deformations of Compactifiable Manifolds
record.context_brief: Rigidity invariant for manifolds with boundary
record.original_question: Is there a numerical invariant for manifolds with boundary that detects rigidity, in the same way that Whitehead torsion detects when an h-cobordism is a cylinder?

evidence.quote: Question 5. Is there a numerical invariant that characterizes when a manifold with boundary is rigid, similarly to the way Whitehead torsion characterizes when an h-cobordism is a cylinder?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A compact manifold with boundary $M$ (with interior $\mathring M$) is said to be rigid if every continuous deformation of its smooth/topological structure (precisely: every one-parameter family of compactifiable manifold structures on $\mathring M$ extending $M$) is, up to an appropriate equivalence, trivial — i.e. $M$ admits no nontrivial deformations as a compactifiable manifold. Recall that the s-cobordism theorem provides a complete numerical/algebraic obstruction to triviality of h-cobordisms: an h-cobordism $(W;M_0,M_1)$ of dimension $\geq 6$ is diffeomorphic to the cylinder $M_0 \times [0,1]$ if and only if its Whitehead torsion $\tau(W,M_0) \in \mathrm{Wh}(\pi_1 M_0)$ vanishes.

Question: Does there exist an analogous invariant — a function $\rho$ assigning to each compact manifold with boundary $M$ an element $\rho(M)$ of some explicitly defined abelian group (or set with distinguished element $0$) — such that $M$ is rigid (in the sense above) if and only if $\rho(M) = 0$? In other words, produce such a "rigidity invariant" for compact manifolds with boundary, or prove that no such invariant exists.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any work proposing or ruling out such a numerical/algebraic rigidity invariant for compactifiable manifolds with boundary in analogy with Whitehead torsion. Standard references discuss Whitehead torsion and the s-cobordism theorem but do not address this specific question, so its current status is unclear.

status_evidence.title: Whitehead torsion - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: An h-cobordism is a cylinder iff its Whitehead torsion vanishes (s-cobordism theorem).
status_evidence.claim: Background confirming the analogy invoked in the problem; no rigidity invariant for manifolds with boundary is mentioned.

status_evidence.title: A simplification problem in manifold theory
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses simplification and rigidity-type problems for manifolds with boundary using Whitehead torsion.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature exists but does not provide a complete numerical rigidity invariant of the type sought.
